## Anti-patterns

- **Skip T1 because edit "looks mechanical"** — empirically refuted: every "mechanical" port edit this fire surfaced 1-6 codex findings on first T1. Mechanical surface ≠ codex-finds-nothing.
- **Skip T1 because the rule itself is about T1** (meta-recursive trap) — empirically caught at iter-9 (n=2 with iter-1 sota-loop-discipline.md v0.1). The rule's authority does NOT exempt the rule from the rule.
- **Trust codex paraphrase of source over actual file** — codex T1 can hallucinate cite line ranges; verify against actual file before applying findings (synthesis-layer-verify recursive application).
- **Layer-fix forever** — escalate to `closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md` Outcome B at round 5 OR confidence escalation between rounds.
- **"Bundle multiple design surfaces in one T1"** — split into per-surface consults; codex narrows better with focused scope (3-axis vs 7-axis from this fire's iter-1 sota-loop-discipline arc).
- **Skip codex when local-judge is "good enough"** — local-judge is failover, not substitute. Cross-model consensus requires GPT-5.5; same-architecture-judge consensus is single-model dressed up.
- **Ship without verdict file referenced in commit body** — the verdict file is the audit trail. Future cycles need to find it. Always cite `.claude/state/codex_consult_<topic>_OUT.txt` or `.claude/state/codex_review_HEAD_<sha>.txt`.
- **Cite commit hashes in stable rule §Related cross-refs** — commit hashes belong in commit messages and provenance, not in cross-rule edges (per iter-8 codex finding).
- **Trust first T1 verdict hit instead of file END** — codex deep-review-exec outputs span 1k-10k lines and routinely echo the `VERDICT:` template near the start before emitting the real verdict at EOF. Discipline: `wc -l <file>` first; `grep -nE "VERDICT:|^F-[0-9]|conf=|confidence|APPROVE|NEEDS-REVISION|REJECT|severity (P[0-3])" <file> | tail -20` (force last hits); then `tail -200 <file>` to confirm final verdict block at EOF. Provenance: `feedback_codex_t1_verdict_reading_discipline.md` + iter-21 fix-forward.

## The rule

    2. **SECONDARY (read-only research)**: cite-anchor TIER-1 SOTA pattern at `Z:/repos/deps/<repo>/<file>:<line> @ HEAD <SHA>` — immutable cite consumed as RESEARCH input per cardinal-rule-9 read-only research probe exception; NOT install-class
    3. **TERTIARY (last-resort exception)**: cite-import-AMBER from sibling claude-sota per Section 14.5 — permitted ONLY when sota-researcher subagent invocation per cardinal-rule-10 step 4 returns **HONEST-NON-FINDING evidence** demonstrating no upstream parity exists for the primitive

    **Cite-import-AMBER is NOT DEFAULT.** Manifest rows MUST satisfy the HONEST-NON-FINDING gate predicate before STAGED → CITE-IMPORT-AMBER promotion (testable):
    - (i) sota-researcher subagent dispatched with explicit upstream-parity-probe scope (probe upstream marketplaces / npm / PyPI / cargo / GitHub repos / Anthropic CC docs / ECC plugin skills / mattpocock-skills / obra-superpowers / anthropic-cookbook for primitive equivalent)
    - (ii) Probe DAG (P1 LICENSE → P2 registry-existence → P3 plugin-namespace → P4 GraphQL stars-and-bands → P5 README/frontmatter → P6 deep audit) per `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/agents/sota-researcher.md` returns NO install-class equivalent
    - (iii) HONEST-NON-FINDING return shape per `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/synthesis-layer-verify.md §Reporting categories`
    - (iv) Manifest row records HNF evidence (sota-researcher dispatch ID + probes + return) in `docs/install-provenance.md` under `effective_tier=TIER-3-LOCAL-COMPOSITION` marker per cardinal-rule-1 cite-class lattice (sibling-derived CANNOT be elevated to TIER-1 SOTA per `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/citation-discipline.md` rule #8)

    **CR-9 install-risk discipline applies at the cite-import fallback layer**: pre-cite-import REVERT check + sibling-bleed defense + version-pin (sibling commit SHA at copy time) + 2-round fix-forward budget. The fallback path is NOT free of CR-9; it inherits ALL CR-9 sub-rules.

    **Operational integration with CR-10 + CR-11**: cardinal-rule-10 step 1 ("(a) Install canonical SOTA solution") preempts step (b)/(c)/(d) under CR-12 — research-first-then-install workflow MUST exhaust upstream-install paths BEFORE classifying as cite-adapt OR best-SOTA-recommended OR HONEST-NON-FINDING. Cardinal-rule-11 META-process: every fire involving sibling-cite-import is gated by upstream-parity probe.

    ### CR-12 disposition lattice (6 classes — Wave 134 Fire 27 series + W152-F20+ CITE-CLASS-CANONICAL codification)

    Beyond the **install-source priority order** (PRIMARY/SECONDARY/TERTIARY) above, every upstream-vs-incumbent relationship falls into ONE of 6 classes. Wave 134 Fire 27 series mapped 5 (classes 1-5 below); W152-F20+ same-arc n=4 evidence promoted CITE-CLASS-CANONICAL as the 6th (per `codification-threshold.md` cycle-321 expected-savings fast-path):

    **Cite class for this 6-class lattice itself**: `constituents=[TIER-3-LOCAL-OPERATOR-DERIVED @ Wave 134 Fire 27-A + 27-B + 27-C codex T1 verdicts, TIER-3-LOCAL-OPERATOR-DERIVED @ W152-F20 + F22 + F23 + F24 same-arc n=4 evidence (commits 4170fbc + 4ed6666 + 04b1eb4 + 1d35a22), TIER-2 @ existing cardinal-rule-12 scaffolding, TIER-2 @ Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/citation-discipline.md rule #8 source-class reduction lattice precedent, TIER-1-DIRECT @ Anthropic + OpenAI + LangChain TIER-1 maintainer evidence]; effective_tier=TIER-3-LOCAL-COMPOSITION` per `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/citation-discipline.md` rule #8 MIN_PRECEDENCE.

# Convergence Gate — Adopt Only When Pattern Has Converged

# TIER-3 port provenance only: ported from Z:/claude/rules/convergence-gate.md HEAD. Parent CCC retains cycle-N audit evidence; claude-sota authority is the TIER-1/TIER-2 sources cited inside this rule.

## The rule
A new pattern, repo, SDK, or external primitive is ADOPT-NOW only when CONVERGENCE evidence is present. Convergence means the pattern exists independently in multiple authoritative places, not just one. Absent convergence, the default verdict is **REJECT-until-convergence** — not STUDY-PILOT, not "maybe later."

This gate stacks ABOVE the `.claude/skills/sota-research/SKILL.md` 5-row LOAD-BEARING bar (LOCAL — sota-research skill present at `.claude/skills/sota-research/SKILL.md`). It is stricter: the 5-row bar allows STUDY-PILOT on any `[UNKNOWN]`; the convergence gate does not — any missing convergence axis is a REJECT until that axis is satisfied OR the STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS predicate fires.

## Convergence axes (ALL three required for ADOPT-NOW)

| Axis | Threshold | Evidence shape |
|---|---|---|
| **Independent T1 sources** | ≥3 distinct orgs/repos/papers implementing the pattern | file:line cites in 3 different `Z:/repos/deps/<repo>/` dirs OR 3 different official docs URLs — not 3 pages of the same source |
| **Named T2 practitioners** | ≥2 named practitioners publicly adopting | Recognizable engineers (Karpathy / Simon Willison / Boris Cherny / Anthropic staff / equivalents), with a dated artifact (tweet, blog post, commit, conf talk) citing THIS specific pattern — not generic category endorsement |
| **Stability** | ≥3 months from pattern emergence to evaluation date | first public commit/post ≥90d old; <90d = "new and shiny," re-evaluate after the burn-in period (UNLESS STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS applies — see §Axis 3 5-band table) |

Any axis failing = REJECT-until-convergence. Verdict line must name the specific missing axis + the exact evidence that would satisfy it.

## Terminology disambiguation

**Convergence-gate Axis 3** = **stability** (age + cpd; quantitative scalar measuring repo/pattern maturity). About: "is this pattern old enough to trust?"

**`.claude/rules/synthesis-layer-verify.md` Subclaim-type discriminator** (UPSTREAM-CLAIM / OPERATIONAL-CLAIM / CATEGORY-CLAIM) = **claim-source classification** (qualitative shape; about what's being verified, not when). About: "which kind of evidence does this claim require?"

Same word "axis" appears in both rules referring to different concepts. Use full names ("Axis 3 stability" vs "subclaim-type discriminator") when ambiguity matters.

## How to apply

Before writing any ADOPT verdict in `reports/sota-*.md` or `reports/*-audit*.md`:

1. **List the 3 T1 sources explicitly**. If you cannot name 3 different `Z:/repos/deps/<repo>/file:line` OR 3 different official docs URLs where the pattern appears independently, the axis fails.
2. **Name the 2 T2 practitioners explicitly with dated artifact**. "Karpathy endorses" without a tweet URL + date is not evidence; it's wishful.
3. **Check the stability clock**. First commit / first public post date — `mcp__github__get_file_contents` on first-commit metadata, or the earliest blog post / paper date. <90d = candidate for STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS only (see §Axis 3); else fail.
4. **If ANY axis fails**, write `REJECT-until-convergence` as the verdict, with a bullet list specifying exactly what evidence would close each missing axis.
5. **Only then** run the sota-research 5-row bar. The convergence gate is a precondition — passing it doesn't auto-ADOPT, but failing it auto-REJECTS.

## Evaluation methodology — concrete tools per axis

Server-family availability per `.claude/rules/research-protocol.md:52-69` Tool Routing (iter-2 port). Function-level support marked `use-if-available` where the iter-2 routing table didn't independently verify the specific call shape.

### Axis 1 — Independent T1 sources (≥3 distinct)

Parallel enumeration via complementary tools — each catches what the others miss:

| Tool family | Strength | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `mcp__github__search_code` / `mcp__github__get_file_contents` | Exact symbol / import-pattern matches across GitHub | ACTIVE |
| `mcp__octocode__githubSearchCode` | Cross-repo code search with stable query identifiers — substitute: `mcp__github__search_code` | REMOVED (2026-05-03 Round-5d; FM-04 D6 firm) |
| `mcp__deepwiki__read_wiki_structure` + `read_wiki_contents` | AI-generated structured wiki per repo — surfaces patterns not in README keywords | ACTIVE (use-if-available; structure/content calls returned 404 on some repos in prior cycles) |
| `mcp__deepwiki__ask_question` | Repo-level Q&A without reading every file | ACTIVE — verify-only, not sole evidence |
| `mcp__repomix__pack_remote_repository` + `grep_repomix_output` | Cross-file pattern scan inside one repo | ACTIVE |
| `mcp__context7__resolve-library-id` + `query-docs` | Official docs as T1 (when adopting a library) | ACTIVE |
| `mcp__exa__web_search_exa` (category:research paper) | Peer-reviewed papers + named-org blogs as T1 | ACTIVE |
| `mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_scrape` / `firecrawl_search` | Live-scrape when target is JS-rendered or behind soft paywall | ACTIVE |

**Rule**: at least 3 of these must return positive evidence for the SAME pattern from 3 DIFFERENT orgs/repos/papers. Not 3 different tools on the same source.

### Axis 2 — Named T2 practitioners (≥2 with dated artifact)

| Tool family | Use | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `mcp__exa__web_search_exa` (category:people, full name + pattern) | Find blog posts / talks by named practitioners | ACTIVE |
| `mcp__perplexity__perplexity_search` (recency filter: month/year) | Fresh endorsements — recognizable practitioners mentioning the pattern | ACTIVE |
| `mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_scrape` on social profiles | Verify a claimed tweet/post actually exists and is dated | ACTIVE |
| `mcp__github__get_me` / search-users / repo collaborator metadata | Employer / org affiliation signals | ACTIVE |
| `mcp__deepwiki__ask_question` on the candidate repo | "Who are the major users or contributors from named orgs?" — triangulate | ACTIVE — use-if-available |

**Mandatory step — WebFetch README + grep practitioners**: GraphQL/`mcp__github__` collaborator metadata is necessary but **not sufficient** for axis 2. Named-practitioner endorsements frequently live in README content (direct quotes, acknowledgments, case studies) rather than repo-collaborator metadata. Before scoring axis 2, ALWAYS:
1. `WebFetch` (or `mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_scrape`) the README
2. Grep for named-practitioner tokens recognizable in the relevant ecosystem
3. Require URL + date on each citation per the base rule

**Bidirectional**: the README-grep step upgrades verdicts when collaborator-metadata missed a signal AND confirms-REJECT when README also shows zero. Without the README-grep step, canonical repos with direct practitioner endorsements can be scored [UNKNOWN] → REJECT incorrectly.

**Rule**: each claimed practitioner endorsement must have a URL + date. "X tweets about Y" without a link is [UNKNOWN], not T2.

### Axis 3 — Stability (≥3 months first-public-artifact age, scored across 5 bands)

| Tool family | Use | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `mcp__github__get_file_contents` / commit history | `createdAt` / first-commit on the repo — repo age | ACTIVE |
| `mcp__exa__web_search_exa` (date range) | Earliest blog post / paper mentioning the pattern | ACTIVE |
| `mcp__arxiv__search_papers` + `get_abstract` | Paper publication date for research-backed patterns | ACTIVE |

**Rule**: 90 days minimum from EARLIEST public artifact, not from the version you're looking at. A v2.0 release isn't stability evidence if v1.0 was 30 days ago.

**Supplementary signal — commits/day (cpd)**: raw age alone under-specifies stability. A 99-day-old repo shipping 15 commits/day is structurally different from a 99-day-old repo shipping 1 commit/week — the former is still in active iteration, not burn-in. Compute `cpd = total_commits / age_days` alongside age:

| cpd × age band | Classification | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| `cpd < 10` AND `age ≥ 90d` | Stable burn-in | Firm axis-3 PASS |
| `10 ≤ cpd ≤ 20` AND `90d ≤ age ≤ 180d` | Active iteration | Borderline axis-3 — PASS-with-caveat; downgrade to STUDY-PILOT or CONDITIONAL-ADOPT if axis-2 also PARTIAL |
| `cpd > 10` AND `age > 180d` | **Sustained active maintenance** | Firm axis-3 PASS — mature age proves stability AND velocity signals ongoing investment, NOT rewrite churn. Classic shape: high-velocity repos past burn-in (avoid misclassifying as fast-churn anti-pattern) |
| `cpd > 10` AND `age < 100d` | Fast-churn anti-pattern | Treat age-PASS as borderline, expect rewrites, re-audit after +90d |
| **STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS** (5th band, predicate-gated): `age ≥ 30d` AND axis-1 = official-org maintainership AND axis-2 = named-T2 endorsement OR maintainer-org IS T2-equivalent | **Firm axis-3 PASS — relaxed maturity gate** | When provenance is strong (org-level T1) AND a named-T2 OR org-equivalent endorsement exists, the launch-spike risk that motivates the strict 90-day gate is dominated by maintainer-org commitment. Examples of org-level T1 patterns: vercel-labs / anthropics / openai / getzep / langchain / microsoft / google / facebook-research / google-deepmind / openai-evals / equivalents. The LAUNCH-SPIKE band still applies for `unknown-org + age<90d + cpd>50` — protection holds for the truly anti-pattern cases (solo-org launch with non-permissive license = REJECT-UNTIL-CONVERGENCE unchanged) |

The bands are exhaustive — every candidate falls into exactly one. STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS is a predicate-gated relaxation, not a default fallback; verify all three predicate clauses (≥30d age, official-org maintainer, named-T2 or org-equivalent endorsement) before applying it.

### Fusion rule (Rider 4 discipline)

No single tool is authoritative. Running any ONE of the above in isolation produces narrow-grep false-negatives (single-tool signal ≠ convergence). The convergence check requires ≥3 distinct tool-types returning compatible evidence — otherwise treat the finding as "one-tool signal," which is not convergence.

Cost discipline: cheap-first. `mcp__github__` calls (cheap, rate-limited) before `mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_agent` (multi-minute credits). DeepWiki `ask_question` before packing the whole repo with repomix. If 3 cheap signals converge, don't escalate to expensive ones; if they don't converge, ONE expensive confirmatory signal is worth more than three more cheap ones.

## Anti-pattern: retroactive convergence manufacturing

Do not construct convergence evidence after choosing the verdict. The sequence must be: (1) collect convergence evidence → (2) count axes → (3) verdict. Not (1) pick verdict → (2) find supporting cites.

If a candidate looks promising but fails convergence today, the right move is to **queue a re-audit date** (90 days out, or when a named T2 practitioner is spotted adopting it), not lower the gate.

## Anti-pattern: Row-2 fabrication-test FAIL

When running the 5-row bar's Row 2 (Numeric — measurable improvement), a README presenting **≥3 numeric performance claims without methodology citation** (no repro script link, no benchmark repo, no dataset name) is **auto-FAIL** — do not attempt live A/B to verify, just REJECT. This short-circuits the primary-source rule: vendor marketing numbers that aren't backed by a reproducible artifact are false-by-default until proven otherwise.

**Procedure**:
1. Count numeric claims in README that make improvement/speedup assertions
2. For each, check: does the README cite a reproducible artifact (benchmark script path, dataset name, tool+version)?
3. If ≥3 claims lack citations, Row-2 auto-FAIL → REJECT verdict bypasses expensive verification step
4. If 1-2 claims lack citations, run the live-verify anyway (lower signal-to-noise)
5. If all claims cite reproducible artifacts, proceed to full primary-source check

**Why auto-FAIL not just downgrade**: across multiple prior live A/B verifications of fabrication-pattern candidates, none survived verification. The prior probability of "≥3 unsourced claims yet verifiable" is empirically near-zero. Running the bench is budget-wasting ritual.

**Three-tier evidence-density ladder** (illustrative exemplars; "evidence-density gradient" = how much reproducible methodology sits behind the numeric claim):

- **Tier 0** (auto-FAIL): `tirth8205/code-review-graph` — ≥3 README numeric claims lack a live methodology artifact; claimed `evaluate/reports/summary.md` absent in verified checkout (numeric claims live in diagrams/tables/narrative) [VERIFIED 2026-05-03 via `Z:/repos/deps/code-review-graph/README.md:32,68,91-104,120-123,146-159,183-194 @ HEAD 0919071a9ba353e604981059e99ee2ed98768092`].
- **Tier 2** (strong-PASS): `context-mode` — `BENCHMARK.md` with 21 fixtures + repro instructions [VERIFIED 2026-05-03 via `Z:/repos/deps/context-mode/BENCHMARK.md:1-16,36-49,59-72,140-172 @ HEAD e40102e534632b137d2b9425b5ddd318222d114e`].
- **Tier 1** (mega-exemplar): `garrytan/gbrain` + `garrytan/gbrain-evals` — separate `gbrain-evals` repo with versioned benchmark scorecards [VERIFIED 2026-05-03 against `gbrain-evals` commit `b8cf8ad057635cbb03c0f3996acb693afbcae605`; see `README.md:5-10,25-45,88-120,151+`, `docs/benchmarks/2026-04-19-brainbench-v0_11-vs-v0_12.md:3-8,35-36,85-99`, `docs/benchmarks/2026-04-18-brainbench-v1.md:6-20,82-106,240-273`].

Use the tier only as a routing hint:
- **Tier 1** (dedicated eval repo): route to §procedure step 5; cite the eval repo and benchmark scorecard.
- **Tier 2** (inline benchmark with real fixtures): route to §procedure step 5; cite the benchmark file and repro commands.
- **Tier 0** (≥3 unsupported numeric claims or broken methodology links): §procedure step 3 AUTO-FAILS; do not spend live-verify budget.

## Even-shorter-path: upstream self-flags impostor-domain risk

If a README opens with a `[!CAUTION] Scam alert` block warning of impostor domains distributing malware, that's a STRONG axis-2 self-flag — the upstream itself is signaling the candidate exists in a high-volume scam-attractor space (typically a viral-young repo where bad actors create lookalike forks). Auto-REJECT axis-2 even before counting unsourced numeric claims.

**How to apply**: when scanning a README for axis-2 named-practitioner endorsements, also scan the FIRST 10 lines for `Scam alert` / `[!CAUTION]` blocks warning of impostor domains. If present, the candidate has been or currently is in a high-attention attractor space — REJECT-until-convergence even if other axes look strong (the self-flag indicates ongoing trust-volatility).

**Distinguishes from §Anti-pattern Row-2 fabrication-test FAIL**: that rule fires on candidate AUTHORS publishing unsourced claims (deception via omission). This rule fires on candidate AUTHORS warning about THIRD-PARTY impostors (deception attractor signal). Same auto-REJECT axis-2 verdict, different mechanism.

- `.claude/rules/evidence-policy.md` Marker Decay corollary: **Marker Decay is claim freshness at reuse time** ("[VERIFIED yesterday] may be [INFERRED] today if upstream changed"). **Convergence-gate Axis 3 stability is adoption maturity** ("repo / pattern is old enough to trust as ADOPT-NOW"). The two are conceptually adjacent — both touch on temporal aspects of evidence — but they are NOT substitutes:

.claude/rules\parallel-session-worktree-isolation.md:115:   - **(c) Lockfile + O_CREAT|O_APPEND atomic-write for SHARED JSONL append**: open the JSONL log with `os.open(path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND | os.O_WRONLY, mode)` where `mode` defaults to `0o600` (owner-only — per Round-5b T3 round-3 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.78 NEW-CLASS trust-boundary finding on commit `c2b5dee`: `0o644` was world-readable and leaked audit-trail content (agent prompts, PIDs, verdict cite paths, `agent_id` UUIDs, T1/T2/T3 verdict bodies) on multi-user hosts. Callers MAY opt-in to `0o640` group-readable for shared-CI cases via explicit `mode=` argument + documented umask interaction (e.g., `umask 0o027` for CI runner) — `0o644` is REJECTED as default for any audit-trail JSONL). **Migration semantic for legacy files** *(Round-7 amendment per T3 round-4 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.91 NEW-CLASS finding on commit `df37fb1`; closes non-migrating gap caught by codex GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE — POSIX `os.open` applies `mode` ONLY when `O_CREAT` actually CREATES the file)*: pre-existing files at `0o644` (created under Round-3-through-5 mandates pre-Round-6) RETAIN their world-readable perms after open, leaving the audit-trail leak intact unless coerced. After every `os.open`, the caller MUST: (i) read `current_mode = stat.S_IMODE(os.fstat(fd).st_mode)`; (ii) if `current_mode != mode` AND the file is owned by caller-uid, call `os.fchmod(fd, mode)` to coerce existing file to the mode invariant; (iii) if `os.fchmod` raises (`PermissionError` due to read-only mount, alien owner, ACL conflict on Windows NTFS, etc.), FAIL CLOSED — propagate the exception rather than proceeding with non-conforming perms (the audit-trail invariant is enforced everywhere or fails loudly). Document in commit body for any consumer applying this rule: one-time migration shell command `find .claude/state -name '*.jsonl' -perm /044 -exec chmod 0600 {} +` (POSIX) OR `Get-ChildItem -Path .claude/state -Filter *.jsonl -Recurse | Where-Object { ($_ | Get-Acl).AccessToString -match 'Everyone Allow Read' } | ForEach-Object { icacls $_.FullName /inheritance:r /grant ${env:USERNAME}:F }` (Windows) for legacy `mcp_health.jsonl` / `subagent_transcripts.jsonl` / `codex_postcommit_reviews.jsonl` / `subagent_start.jsonl` / `worktree_lifecycle_audit.jsonl` files created at `0o644` per pre-Round-6 mandates. The `O_CREAT` flag ensures a missing log auto-creates rather than failing the first writer; **if `os.open` raises (read-only mount, permission denied, disk full), the exception MUST propagate — do not catch-and-ignore** (per Round-5 F-1 silent-failure finding). Take an **exclusive advisory lock** (`fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX)` on POSIX / `msvcrt.locking` on Windows); **if neither primitive is available, or if the platform does not enforce advisory locks (e.g., NFS without NLM support), FAIL CLOSED — raise rather than proceeding without a lock** (per Round-5 F-2 NFS-silent-succeed finding). **Windows separate-lockfile mechanism** *(Round-7c per T3 round-7b NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.78 NEW-CLASS finding on commit `48c49fb` caught by codex GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE)*: `msvcrt.locking` locks `nbytes` from CURRENT file-pointer position, NOT the whole file like POSIX `fcntl.flock`. Under O_APPEND the JSONL fd's pointer moves on each write, breaking lock-release symmetry (LK_UNLCK at the new pointer would find no lock at the byte LK_LOCK was issued for). Round-7b workaround (shipped at `scripts/_atomic_jsonl_append.py:_acquire_lock(fd, path)` commit `48c49fb`): open separate `<jsonl-path>.lock` file with 1-byte placeholder + lock byte 0 of the LOCKFILE (no writes to lockfile means file pointer stays at byte 0). Module returns `lock_fd` for Windows callers to release; `None` for POSIX. **Lock-protocol rollout constraint** *(Round-7c per same T3 finding)*: when the lock protocol bumps (direct-jsonl-fd → separate-lockfile-v1, or separate-lockfile-v1 → separate-lockfile-v2-versioned), enforce single-version deployment for the entire concurrent-writer cohort. Old + new code locking DIFFERENT lock domains do NOT mutually exclude — concurrent writers can race even though each ALONE acquires its lock correctly. Mitigations (pick ONE before any concurrent rollout): **(i) transitional dual-lock**: acquire both old AND new protocol locks in series during the transition window; **(ii) runtime version-marker**: write protocol-version byte to lockfile + fail-closed on read-version-mismatch (FORWARD-REF for v2 lock protocol bump); **(iii) single-version cohort barrier**: coordinate cohort upgrade via deployment system before any new-version runs. Currently sss has ZERO consumers of `_atomic_jsonl_append.py` (FORWARD-REF wire-up Ships 2-5 pending per `tmp/wave22-orchestrator-salvage-jsonl-mode-bits-audit-2026-05-05.md`), so the version-skew window is THEORETICAL until first hook migrates to use the module. Future protocol bumps MUST honor one of (i)/(ii)/(iii). HOLD the lock across BOTH (a) JSON-encoding the record AND (b) the single low-level `os.write(fd, encoded_bytes)` — never use buffered text writes (`f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")` via Python file objects can split into multiple writes). **If JSON encoding raises (`UnicodeEncodeError`, non-serializable type), release the lock and propagate the exception — do not silently drop the record** (per Round-5 F-3 silent-record-drop finding). For records where **`len(encoded_bytes)` — the byte count AFTER JSON encoding, NOT the key count of the dict —** exceeds the platform atomic-write bound (≤PIPE_BUF 4KB POSIX; ≤512 bytes for Windows or treat the lock as the sole correctness boundary), reject the record OR shard via option (b) filename-namespace; do NOT silently truncate (per Round-5 F-5 measurement-target finding). After the write, `os.fsync(fd)` if durability is part of the contract (audit-trail JSONL needs fsync; ephemeral telemetry may skip); **if `os.fsync` raises (`EIO`, `ENOSPC`), propagate the exception — do not silently ignore a durability failure when durability is contracted** (per Round-5 F-4 fsync-failure finding). Use for SHARED JSONL log targets (`mcp_health.jsonl`, `subagent_transcripts.jsonl`, `codex_postcommit_reviews.jsonl` class) where consumers expect interleaved appends from multiple writers and unified-view semantics are required.

19:Every SOTA-research fire (sota-researcher dispatch / repo evaluation / candidate audit / convergence verification / replacement consideration) MUST query **≥4 distinct sources** from the discovery cohort below. Single-source convergence is FRAGILE and produces false-confidence verdicts. Discovery breadth is the input-side analog of `convergence-gate.md` Axis-1 ≥3-distinct-orgs output-side requirement.

21:## Discovery cohort (≥4 distinct source FAMILIES required per fire)
22:
23:**Distinct source definition** (per Pattern A codex T1 Fire 29a prescriptions #1+#2+#6): A "distinct source" is a distinct **backend / data corpus / provider**, NOT a tool endpoint. Multiple MCP endpoints OR CLI commands under the SAME provider count as ONE source family. Example: `mcp__github__search_repositories` + `mcp__github__search_code` + `mcp__github__list_commits` + `gh CLI` all count as ONE source (GitHub).

44:### Counting rules (per codex T1 Fire 29a prescription #5)
45:
46:- **ALREADY-INSTALLED + WIRED sources** may count any time queried with relevant results
47:- **NOT-WIRED sources** count ONLY when queried via documented working alternate path (WebFetch / HTTP-direct / ctx_fetch_and_index) AND return relevant results
48:- **REFERENCE-ONLY catalogs** count ONLY when they return RELEVANT candidate evidence (per failure-mode #2: catalogs are discovery hints, not quality verdicts)
49:- **Multiple endpoints / sub-capabilities under one provider** count as ONE source family (GitHub family contains gh CLI + ~30+ MCP endpoints; DeepWiki family contains 3 MCP endpoints; all sub-capabilities collapse to ONE count)
50:- **Source must return ≥1 relevant candidate** OR explicit HONEST-NON-FINDING to count toward the ≥4 gate
51:
52:## How to apply
53:
54:For every SOTA-research fire:
55:
56:1. **List discovery sources used** explicitly in the fire's tracker.md or close-synthesis.md (e.g., "Discovery sources: GitHub MCP / Exa MCP / DeepWiki MCP / Perplexity MCP / Brave Search via WebFetch")
57:2. **Verify ≥4 distinct sources** were queried before any candidate ranking/verdict
58:3. **Score discovery breadth in SRA verdict** (forward-ref to SRA D11 when codified): ≥4 sources = PASS / <4 sources = DOWNGRADE-WITH-DISCLOSURE
59:4. **Document HONEST-NON-FINDING** if a source returned no relevant results — that IS the deliverable; do NOT silently drop the source
60:5. **Per-source result-trust hierarchy** (forward-ref to IMP-K source-quality scoring when codified — Fire 29b candidate):
61:   - TIER-1-OFFICIAL named-org first-party API (GitHub / arXiv / deps.dev) > community catalog > scraped HTML
62:   - Discovery breadth COUNT × source QUALITY = effective breadth signal (not just raw count)
63:
64:## Why
65:
66:User-doc 9-layer architecture §Dimension A explicitly notes "**The discovery layer must be polyglot.** GitHub MCP alone is not enough." Empirical evidence cited in user-doc:
67:- OSSInsight 10B GitHub events surface trending NOT visible via GitHub search alone
68:- Star History time-decay reveals "fresh-paint" anti-pattern that raw star count hides
69:- deps.dev transitive view exposes license + CVE risk invisible to README scan
70:- Snyk Advisor's 4-category scoring smooths popularity-bias that single-source counts amplify
71:- DeepWiki auto-generated wikis cover 50K+ repos with structured Q&A vs raw README
72:
73:Single-source narrow-grep produces:
74:- False-negatives (legitimate SOTA candidates missed because they don't surface in GitHub search alone)
75:- False-positives (high-star repos that fail Scorecard / fail OSV / have stale maintenance)
76:- Bias toward TypeScript/JavaScript ecosystem (GitHub-default search weights newer + popular)
77:
78:## When NOT to apply
79:
80:- **Targeted re-verification of a NAMED candidate** (e.g., "verify gitnexus@1.6.4-rc.112 still maintains polyforge-noncommercial license") — single-source GitHub MCP query suffices because the target is named, not discovered
81:- **Fix-forward / Pattern A apply** on existing codex T1 verdict — no new discovery needed; the verdict's prescriptions are the input
82:- **Mia pre-apply probe** on a single agent prescription — Mia is verification not discovery
83:- **Hook script / settings.json maintenance** — no SOTA research involved
84:- **Trivial doc-typo / cite-line fixes** — discovery N/A
85:
86:## Anti-patterns
87:
88:- **GitHub-only search** — refuted by user-doc §Dimension A "the discovery layer must be polyglot"; produces bias toward TypeScript/JavaScript + recent + popular
89:- **Awesome-list bloat** — refuted by user-doc failure-mode #2; treat awesome lists as discovery hint only, never as quality verdict
90:- **Star count as sufficient signal** — refuted by user-doc + Fire 28 IMP-K (source-quality > raw count); also refuted by `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/convergence-gate.md` Axis 3 fresh-paint anti-pattern
91:- **Source-count without verifying RELEVANT results** — running 4 different MCP queries that all return "no results" does NOT satisfy this gate; ≥4 sources MUST each return at least ONE relevant candidate (or HONEST-NON-FINDING explicit)
92:- **Skip the ≥4 gate because "I know the candidate already"** — refuted by Fire 27-C mem0 retro: orchestrator pre-audit ASSUMED Fire 27-B sqlite-vec finding might apply to mem0 (single-source assumption); codex T1 REFUTED; per-fire ≥4 verification mandatory regardless of prior-fire confidence
93:- **Treating ALREADY-INSTALLED candidates as "no need to research"** — refuted by Wave 144 Fire 1 astral-sh/uv RECLASSIFY: candidate was ALREADY-INSTALLED-VIA-SYSTEM-PATH but manifest stale; periodic re-discovery via multi-source gate catches drift
94:- **Counting multiple endpoints from one provider as multiple distinct sources** (per Pattern A codex T1 Fire 29a prescription #6) — refuted by §Discovery cohort "Distinct source definition" + §Counting rules: a single provider (GitHub / DeepWiki / Exa / Context7 / repomix) collapses ALL its sub-capabilities into ONE source-family count. Example anti-pattern: querying `mcp__github__search_repositories` + `mcp__github__search_code` + `mcp__github__list_commits` + `gh CLI repo view` and claiming "4 sources" — actual count = 1 source (GitHub family). Must query ≥4 DIFFERENT provider families.
95:- **Counting INSTALLED-NOT-WIRED sources as available without verifying alternate path** (per Pattern A codex T1 Fire 29a prescription #4+#5) — refuted by §Counting rules: NOT-WIRED sources require documented working alternate path (WebFetch / HTTP-direct / ctx_fetch_and_index) AND relevant-results return. Example anti-pattern: Perplexity@0.8.4 npm-global is INSTALLED but NOT in current .mcp.json; cannot count as "MCP source" until either wired OR queried via WebFetch fallback with relevant results.
96:
97:## Sister-rule integration
98:

 succeeded in 377ms:
21:A new pattern, repo, SDK, or external primitive is ADOPT-NOW only when CONVERGENCE evidence is present. Convergence means the pattern exists independently in multiple authoritative places, not just one. Absent convergence, the default verdict is **REJECT-until-convergence** — not STUDY-PILOT, not "maybe later."
22:
23:This gate stacks ABOVE the `.claude/skills/sota-research/SKILL.md` 5-row LOAD-BEARING bar (LOCAL — sota-research skill present at `.claude/skills/sota-research/SKILL.md`). It is stricter: the 5-row bar allows STUDY-PILOT on any `[UNKNOWN]`; the convergence gate does not — any missing convergence axis is a REJECT until that axis is satisfied OR the STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS predicate fires.
24:
25:## Convergence axes (ALL three required for ADOPT-NOW)
26:
27:| Axis | Threshold | Evidence shape |
28:|---|---|---|
29:| **Independent T1 sources** | ≥3 distinct orgs/repos/papers implementing the pattern | file:line cites in 3 different `Z:/repos/deps/<repo>/` dirs OR 3 different official docs URLs — not 3 pages of the same source |
30:| **Named T2 practitioners** | ≥2 named practitioners publicly adopting | Recognizable engineers (Karpathy / Simon Willison / Boris Cherny / Anthropic staff / equivalents), with a dated artifact (tweet, blog post, commit, conf talk) citing THIS specific pattern — not generic category endorsement |
31:| **Stability** | ≥3 months from pattern emergence to evaluation date | first public commit/post ≥90d old; <90d = "new and shiny," re-evaluate after the burn-in period (UNLESS STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS applies — see §Axis 3 5-band table) |
32:
33:Any axis failing = REJECT-until-convergence. Verdict line must name the specific missing axis + the exact evidence that would satisfy it.
34:
35:## Terminology disambiguation
36:
37:**Convergence-gate Axis 3** = **stability** (age + cpd; quantitative scalar measuring repo/pattern maturity). About: "is this pattern old enough to trust?"
38:
39:**`.claude/rules/synthesis-layer-verify.md` Subclaim-type discriminator** (UPSTREAM-CLAIM / OPERATIONAL-CLAIM / CATEGORY-CLAIM) = **claim-source classification** (qualitative shape; about what's being verified, not when). About: "which kind of evidence does this claim require?"
40:
41:Same word "axis" appears in both rules referring to different concepts. Use full names ("Axis 3 stability" vs "subclaim-type discriminator") when ambiguity matters.
42:
43:## How to apply
44:
45:Before writing any ADOPT verdict in `reports/sota-*.md` or `reports/*-audit*.md`:
46:
47:1. **List the 3 T1 sources explicitly**. If you cannot name 3 different `Z:/repos/deps/<repo>/file:line` OR 3 different official docs URLs where the pattern appears independently, the axis fails.
48:2. **Name the 2 T2 practitioners explicitly with dated artifact**. "Karpathy endorses" without a tweet URL + date is not evidence; it's wishful.
49:3. **Check the stability clock**. First commit / first public post date — `mcp__github__get_file_contents` on first-commit metadata, or the earliest blog post / paper date. <90d = candidate for STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS only (see §Axis 3); else fail.
50:4. **If ANY axis fails**, write `REJECT-until-convergence` as the verdict, with a bullet list specifying exactly what evidence would close each missing axis.
51:5. **Only then** run the sota-research 5-row bar. The convergence gate is a precondition — passing it doesn't auto-ADOPT, but failing it auto-REJECTS.

53:## Evaluation methodology — concrete tools per axis
54:
55:Server-family availability per `.claude/rules/research-protocol.md:52-69` Tool Routing (iter-2 port). Function-level support marked `use-if-available` where the iter-2 routing table didn't independently verify the specific call shape.
56:
57:### Axis 1 — Independent T1 sources (≥3 distinct)
58:
59:Parallel enumeration via complementary tools — each catches what the others miss:
60:
61:| Tool family | Strength | Status |
62:|---|---|---|
63:| `mcp__github__search_code` / `mcp__github__get_file_contents` | Exact symbol / import-pattern matches across GitHub | ACTIVE |
64:| `mcp__octocode__githubSearchCode` | Cross-repo code search with stable query identifiers — substitute: `mcp__github__search_code` | REMOVED (2026-05-03 Round-5d; FM-04 D6 firm) |
65:| `mcp__deepwiki__read_wiki_structure` + `read_wiki_contents` | AI-generated structured wiki per repo — surfaces patterns not in README keywords | ACTIVE (use-if-available; structure/content calls returned 404 on some repos in prior cycles) |
66:| `mcp__deepwiki__ask_question` | Repo-level Q&A without reading every file | ACTIVE — verify-only, not sole evidence |
67:| `mcp__repomix__pack_remote_repository` + `grep_repomix_output` | Cross-file pattern scan inside one repo | ACTIVE |
68:| `mcp__context7__resolve-library-id` + `query-docs` | Official docs as T1 (when adopting a library) | ACTIVE |
69:| `mcp__exa__web_search_exa` (category:research paper) | Peer-reviewed papers + named-org blogs as T1 | ACTIVE |
70:| `mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_scrape` / `firecrawl_search` | Live-scrape when target is JS-rendered or behind soft paywall | ACTIVE |
71:
72:**Rule**: at least 3 of these must return positive evidence for the SAME pattern from 3 DIFFERENT orgs/repos/papers. Not 3 different tools on the same source.
73:
74:### Axis 2 — Named T2 practitioners (≥2 with dated artifact)
75:
76:| Tool family | Use | Status |
77:|---|---|---|
78:| `mcp__exa__web_search_exa` (category:people, full name + pattern) | Find blog posts / talks by named practitioners | ACTIVE |
79:| `mcp__perplexity__perplexity_search` (recency filter: month/year) | Fresh endorsements — recognizable practitioners mentioning the pattern | ACTIVE |
80:| `mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_scrape` on social profiles | Verify a claimed tweet/post actually exists and is dated | ACTIVE |
81:| `mcp__github__get_me` / search-users / repo collaborator metadata | Employer / org affiliation signals | ACTIVE |
82:| `mcp__deepwiki__ask_question` on the candidate repo | "Who are the major users or contributors from named orgs?" — triangulate | ACTIVE — use-if-available |
83:
84:**Mandatory step — WebFetch README + grep practitioners**: GraphQL/`mcp__github__` collaborator metadata is necessary but **not sufficient** for axis 2. Named-practitioner endorsements frequently live in README content (direct quotes, acknowledgments, case studies) rather than repo-collaborator metadata. Before scoring axis 2, ALWAYS:
85:1. `WebFetch` (or `mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_scrape`) the README
86:2. Grep for named-practitioner tokens recognizable in the relevant ecosystem
87:3. Require URL + date on each citation per the base rule
88:
89:**Bidirectional**: the README-grep step upgrades verdicts when collaborator-metadata missed a signal AND confirms-REJECT when README also shows zero. Without the README-grep step, canonical repos with direct practitioner endorsements can be scored [UNKNOWN] → REJECT incorrectly.
90:
91:**Rule**: each claimed practitioner endorsement must have a URL + date. "X tweets about Y" without a link is [UNKNOWN], not T2.
92:
93:### Axis 3 — Stability (≥3 months first-public-artifact age, scored across 5 bands)
94:
95:| Tool family | Use | Status |
96:|---|---|---|
97:| `mcp__github__get_file_contents` / commit history | `createdAt` / first-commit on the repo — repo age | ACTIVE |
98:| `mcp__exa__web_search_exa` (date range) | Earliest blog post / paper mentioning the pattern | ACTIVE |
99:| `mcp__arxiv__search_papers` + `get_abstract` | Paper publication date for research-backed patterns | ACTIVE |
100:
101:**Rule**: 90 days minimum from EARLIEST public artifact, not from the version you're looking at. A v2.0 release isn't stability evidence if v1.0 was 30 days ago.
102:
103:**Supplementary signal — commits/day (cpd)**: raw age alone under-specifies stability. A 99-day-old repo shipping 15 commits/day is structurally different from a 99-day-old repo shipping 1 commit/week — the former is still in active iteration, not burn-in. Compute `cpd = total_commits / age_days` alongside age:
104:
105:| cpd × age band | Classification | Implication |
106:|---|---|---|
107:| `cpd < 10` AND `age ≥ 90d` | Stable burn-in | Firm axis-3 PASS |
108:| `10 ≤ cpd ≤ 20` AND `90d ≤ age ≤ 180d` | Active iteration | Borderline axis-3 — PASS-with-caveat; downgrade to STUDY-PILOT or CONDITIONAL-ADOPT if axis-2 also PARTIAL |
109:| `cpd > 10` AND `age > 180d` | **Sustained active maintenance** | Firm axis-3 PASS — mature age proves stability AND velocity signals ongoing investment, NOT rewrite churn. Classic shape: high-velocity repos past burn-in (avoid misclassifying as fast-churn anti-pattern) |
110:| `cpd > 10` AND `age < 100d` | Fast-churn anti-pattern | Treat age-PASS as borderline, expect rewrites, re-audit after +90d |
111:| **STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS** (5th band, predicate-gated): `age ≥ 30d` AND axis-1 = official-org maintainership AND axis-2 = named-T2 endorsement OR maintainer-org IS T2-equivalent | **Firm axis-3 PASS — relaxed maturity gate** | When provenance is strong (org-level T1) AND a named-T2 OR org-equivalent endorsement exists, the launch-spike risk that motivates the strict 90-day gate is dominated by maintainer-org commitment. Examples of org-level T1 patterns: vercel-labs / anthropics / openai / getzep / langchain / microsoft / google / facebook-research / google-deepmind / openai-evals / equivalents. The LAUNCH-SPIKE band still applies for `unknown-org + age<90d + cpd>50` — protection holds for the truly anti-pattern cases (solo-org launch with non-permissive license = REJECT-UNTIL-CONVERGENCE unchanged) |
112:
113:The bands are exhaustive — every candidate falls into exactly one. STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS is a predicate-gated relaxation, not a default fallback; verify all three predicate clauses (≥30d age, official-org maintainer, named-T2 or org-equivalent endorsement) before applying it.
114:
115:### Fusion rule (Rider 4 discipline)
116:
117:No single tool is authoritative. Running any ONE of the above in isolation produces narrow-grep false-negatives (single-tool signal ≠ convergence). The convergence check requires ≥3 distinct tool-types returning compatible evidence — otherwise treat the finding as "one-tool signal," which is not convergence.
118:
119:Cost discipline: cheap-first. `mcp__github__` calls (cheap, rate-limited) before `mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_agent` (multi-minute credits). DeepWiki `ask_question` before packing the whole repo with repomix. If 3 cheap signals converge, don't escalate to expensive ones; if they don't converge, ONE expensive confirmatory signal is worth more than three more cheap ones.
120:
121:## Anti-pattern: retroactive convergence manufacturing
122:
123:Do not construct convergence evidence after choosing the verdict. The sequence must be: (1) collect convergence evidence → (2) count axes → (3) verdict. Not (1) pick verdict → (2) find supporting cites.
124:
125:If a candidate looks promising but fails convergence today, the right move is to **queue a re-audit date** (90 days out, or when a named T2 practitioner is spotted adopting it), not lower the gate.

31:### The mandate
32:
33:A `gpt5-reviewer` / `gpt5-archaeologist` dispatch under env-funneling MUST do ONE of:
34:
35:1. **(Default)** Return `VERDICT: BLOCK` per the agent's fail-closed contract at `.claude/agents/gpt5-reviewer.md` frontmatter. Stand-in dispatch does NOT satisfy the cross-model gate; BLOCK is the safe action under structural same-model degradation.
36:2. **(Explicit-disclosure)** Return APPROVE / NEEDS-REVISION / REJECT WITH explicit `STAND-IN-NOTICE: agent ran under CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=<model> stand-in per CLAUDE.local.md ENV block (f); cross-model gate NOT structurally satisfied for this dispatch` in the verdict body's first 5 lines. The orchestrator then bears the integration decision: re-fire via real codex CLI, accept stand-in verdict with documented gate-bypass rationale, or REVERT-AND-REMOVE per `closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md` Outcome B.

43:# TIER-3 local codification provenance only: this rule was promoted from `synthesis-layer-verify.md §Pre-apply Mia rule on agent ship-prescriptions` sub-section (Wave 14 codification commit `10d9455` 2026-05-04) to standalone rule after n=8 cumulative dogfood.
44:
45:When an agent (architect / codex T1 prescription / sota-researcher / Explore / general-purpose / codex-rescue / gpt5-reviewer) returns a ship-prescription with `prescribed_edits` / specific file:line claims about gaps to close, **pre-apply the Mia rule (verify against runtime state) BEFORE writing any Edit**. The agent's prescription IS NOT TRUSTED until verified — even when conf ≥ 0.90 + Pattern A trigger.
46:
47:The pattern: **AGENT reads brief context but DOES NOT probe runtime state → produces CATEGORY-CLAIM that LOOKS LIKE OPERATIONAL-CLAIM** (per `synthesis-layer-verify.md §Subclaim-type discriminator`). Agents systematically conflate "should be wired" with "is wired", "should be 80" with "is 80", "is unwired" with "is wired", without checking actual state via `git log` / `Grep` / `Glob`. This rule converts post-hoc OVER detection (existing `synthesis-layer-verify.md §Reporting categories` shape) into PRE-emptive verification (this rule's shape) BEFORE any Edit fires.
48:
49:## When this rule applies
50:
51:Trigger on **prescription shape, regardless of file class**. Apply to actionable prescription shapes:
52:
53:- `prescribed_edits` listing specific file:line + content gaps
54:- gap-claim ("X is unwired" / "X is missing" / "X needs adding")
55:- quantitative claim ("70→80" / "12 files" / "5 hooks")
56:- status flip ("X is FORWARD-REF; promote to ACTIVE")
57:
58:Do **NOT** apply to (avoid paying the discipline tax on non-actionable returns):
59:
60:- Pure analysis returns (no `prescribed_edits` / no concrete file:line claim)
61:- Pure HONEST-NON-FINDING returns (agent already probed and found nothing)
62:- Pure read-only review output (gpt5-reviewer audit summary without specific edits)
63:
64:## How to apply (BEFORE writing any Edit)
65:
66:For each prescription:
67:
68:1. **Decompose the gap-claim** into testable sub-claims (per `synthesis-layer-verify.md §Within-cycle revision discipline (axis-9)`)
69:2. **Pick the cheapest probe per sub-claim** (the §Subclaim-type discriminator informs probe-type selection):
70:   - File-existence claim → `Glob` or `ls -la`
71:   - Line-content claim → `Read <path>:<lines>` or `Grep`
72:   - Wire-status claim → `Grep <hook-name> .claude/settings.json`
73:   - Closed-loop arc claim → `git log --grep="<surface>" --oneline`
74:   - Count claim → actual `wc -l` / `Grep -c` not memory
75:   - SHAPE-CLAIM (settings.json hook entry / .mcp.json server / hook JSONL payload) → `Grep` + schema-validate per `synthesis-layer-verify.md §Output-form verification modifier`
76:3. **Verify EACH sub-claim**. If ≥1 sub-claim refuted → CATEGORY-CLAIM drift detected
77:4. **Classify a refuted gap-prescription as OVER and drop it.** Reserve HONEST-NON-FINDING for an agent/operator report that explicitly probed an assumed target and found no such target (per `synthesis-layer-verify.md §Reporting categories` OVER vs HNF distinction). Do NOT silently apply the prescription; document the refutation in commit body
78:5. **Apply only the verified-surviving prescriptions** in the single atomic Pattern A fix-forward commit per `.claude/rules/codex-t1-fix-forward-pattern.md §Pattern A` — this rule is an admissibility filter BEFORE Pattern A's atomic-apply step (first drop OVER prescriptions, then apply all surviving verified prescriptions atomically)

104:uv tool list 2>/dev/null | grep -i <cli>        # uv tool registry

33:## The rule
34:
35:Every non-trivial fire (architecture audit / SOTA convergence / token-eff investigation / cross-model verification / gap-resolution wave) MUST spawn a 3-5 agent team. **Scope**: output fires only — rule-edit fires are governed by `cross-model-consensus.md` T1/T2/T3 gates alone, not this standing directive. **CADP cap**: concurrent dispatch is bounded by `parallel-agent-wave.md §CADP rule 2` (max 3 concurrent unless `python Z:/claude/ccc/tools/status.py` shows cache ≥50% verified); 4-5 agents MUST use staggered dispatch — see §Anti-patterns for the full CADP carve-out. The team MUST satisfy ALL of:
36:
37:1. **GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE for ≥2 agents** — `codex-rescue` / `gpt5-reviewer` / `gpt5-archaeologist` (Sonnet wrapper invoking real GPT-5.5 via codex CLI); satisfies cross-model-asymmetry per `cross-model-consensus.md`. **Per-call codex time-budget mandate** (Wave 44 FM-17.d codification, refined Wave 45 Fire 1 per codex T1 NEEDS-REVISION conf=0.84 Pattern A): each codex call within agent brief MUST budget time per call -- **default 90s, normal cap 120s, 180s only with explicit reason**. Bounded, independently answerable calls preferred over one xhigh open-ended call when the question decomposes cleanly; keep one call when setup/context dominates OR the answer requires integrated judgment. Wrapper stream-watchdog 600s timeout fires before xhigh codex completion (empirical 5-15min per `cross-model-consensus.md §Profile selection rule`); short-call budget bypasses watchdog OR enables main-session foreground+tee fallback per `fm17-subagent-fleet-depletion.md §FM-17.d` recovery
38:2. **Brief cites SOTA repos at file:line depth** — every claim in the agent brief carries `Z:/repos/deps/<repo>/<file>:<line> @ HEAD <SHA>` OR `code.claude.com/docs/...` OR `mcp__github__get_file_contents` result; agent briefs ARE inputs to the agent's reasoning per `feedback_agent_team_brief_must_cite_sota_repos_at_file_line_2026_05_02.md`
39:3. **Line-by-line SOTA repo audit mandate** — for adoption-class waves, agents must Read the candidate repo's relevant `<file>` end-to-end (NOT skim README); Probe DAG 1-7 per `agent-harness-fit-verification.md`
40:4. **Anthropic official docs as authority guide** — `code.claude.com/docs/en/*` is TIER-1 LIVING-AUTHORITY per `cross-model-consensus.md` Normative Authority Map; CCBP `Z:/repos/deps/claude-code-best-practice-shan/` HEAD-pinned is TIER-2 third-party reinforcement
41:5. **ARTIFACT-INLINE per FM-19** — Bash-only / no-Write agents (architect / gpt5-reviewer / gpt5-archaeologist / code-reviewer) embed `## ARTIFACT-INLINE: tmp/wave<N>-<agent>-<topic>-<date>.md` in final return; orchestrator persists post-completion per `fm19-readonly-guard-sidestep.md`

31:## How to apply (4-axis probe)
32:
33:Before declaring an agent's ship-candidate "ready":
34:
35:### Probe 1 — count-OVER
36:
37:If the candidate claims a count delta (commit count, file count, line count, star count): verify against authoritative local source (`git log`, `wc -l`, `Glob | wc -l`, `mcp__github__search_repositories` star refresh) BEFORE accepting. Agent counts via remote APIs can drift, paginate-truncate, or include stale cache.
38:
39:### Probe 2 — SDK-vs-CLI surface
40:
41:If the candidate proposes adopting an SDK feature / config flag / env var: verify the **invocation surface** exists in claude-sota:
42:- Does claude-sota use the SDK or CLI? Check `.claude/hooks/scripts/*.py` + `.claude/settings.json` env block
43:- Does the candidate's mechanism map to claude-sota's actual mode (interactive vs print-mode vs SDK-managed-agent)?
44:- If the candidate requires a mode claude-sota doesn't run in, REJECT-for-fit even if SOTA-valid upstream
45:
46:### Probe 3 — architectural-API
47:
48:If the candidate proposes a primitive (cache_control, prompt-cache, structured-outputs, batch-API): verify the **API ecosystem match**:
49:- Anthropic-API primitive vs OpenAI-API primitive vs vendor-neutral OTel
50:- claude-sota's gpt5.5/codex hooks talk to OpenAI-API endpoints; Anthropic-only primitives don't apply there
51:- Cross-check before assuming "this Anthropic pattern works on codex"
52:
53:### Probe 5 — mode-harness-shape
54:
55:If the candidate proposes adopting a skill/workflow/pattern with operational mode dependencies (HARD-GATE on user interaction, interactive-vs-autonomous mismatch, meta-skill assumptions about sister-harness presence, file-count or size-sprawl orthogonal to existing layout): verify the **operational mode + harness shape match**:
56:- Does the candidate skill HARD-GATE on interactive user approval? Verify against claude-sota's autonomous /loop mode (incompatible)
57:- Does the candidate require a sister-skill or sister-harness present in upstream's framework but absent locally? (e.g., Superpowers TDD-for-skills test framework)
58:- Does verbatim port introduce file count or size disproportionate to existing layer? (e.g., a single skill bringing 7+ files when sibling skills are 1-3 files)
59:- If ANY mode/harness assumption is unmet, REJECT-FOR-FIT even if SOTA-valid upstream + Axis 1+2+3 PASS

61:### Probe 4 — plugin-namespace
62:
63:If the candidate proposes vendoring an artifact from upstream (ECC, codex-plugin-cc, anthropics-cookbook): check **plugin-loaded skill namespace** FIRST:

61:## Reporting categories — OVER, UNDER, HONEST-NON-FINDING
62:
63:Ship-reports fall into three reporting categories at the synthesis layer, each with a distinct recovery pattern. The categories are exhaustive — every report fits one — and the recovery action differs by category.
64:
65:| Category | Definition | Synthesis-layer response |
66:|---|---|---|
67:| **OVER** | Report claims more than git shows (claimed edit reverted; claimed file absent) | `git reflog` + infrastructure event log; investigate before re-spawn or commit |
68:| **UNDER** | Report claims less than git shows (claimed nothing, file landed; partial credit) | `git diff` to surface the orphan change; accept work + correct report → commit |
69:| **HONEST-NON-FINDING** | Report says "I probed for X, found nothing" — when the brief assumed X exists | Pivot ship — DROP / REDIRECT / amend brief. The HNF IS the deliverable; do NOT re-spawn the agent to "find X anyway" |
70:
71:**Why HNF matters**: it's the highest-value report shape but easiest to mistake for "agent failed to ship." An agent that probes the brief's assumption and finds it wrong has saved a wrong-direction ship — that's a SUCCESS at the discipline layer, not a failure. The synthesis-layer recovery is to update the brief / drop the patch / redirect to the correct target — never to re-spawn under the same (now-refuted) assumption.
72:
73:**HNF as cite-vs-concept sibling**: HNF reports are often the empirical refutation of a brief-level cite-vs-concept failure. Brief asserts X exists at file:line; agent probes; X doesn't exist. Brief's assumption was a CONCEPT (loose familiarity) not a CITE (verified file:line). HNF surfaces this gap. (Cite-vs-concept semantic-equivalence remains FORWARD-REF in claude-sota; the parent CCC narrative is TIER-3 provenance only until ported with TIER-1/TIER-2 backing.)
74:
75:## Subclaim-type discriminator (UPSTREAM / OPERATIONAL / CATEGORY)
76:
77:When applying within-cycle-revision-discipline to a freshness-audit candidate, classify the SUBCLAIM by type BEFORE allocating probe budget. Three categorical types; the type predicts probe yield.
78:
79:| Subclaim type | Definition | Probe yield |
80:|---|---|---|
81:| **UPSTREAM-CLAIM** | About external project's state (README content, repo metadata, framing) — subject to upstream evolution between verdict-cycle and probe-cycle | HIGH refutation candidate — upstream may have reformed |
82:| **OPERATIONAL-CLAIM** | About OUR harness state (live MCP invocations, hook-fire counts, integration depth) — controlled by us, slow-moving | LOW refutation likelihood — state changes only when we change it |
83:| **CATEGORY-CLAIM** | About semantic mismatch between candidate and our use-case (RAG vs session-memory, batch vs streaming) — requires upstream pivot to flip | LOW refutation likelihood — categorical signals stable |
84:
85:**Mixed types**: a single candidate's subclaim chain can include all three. CATEGORY-CLAIM ("API-redundant with X") + OPERATIONAL-CLAIM ("our X integration is live") can both apply to the same exclusion verdict.
86:
87:**How to apply (pre-probe budget allocation)**:
88:1. Type the claim — UPSTREAM / OPERATIONAL / CATEGORY?
89:2. Estimate probe budget — UPSTREAM gets full 5-axis (WebFetch README + GitHub API + convergence-gate axes); OPERATIONAL gets spot-check via local grep; CATEGORY gets one-pass README scan
90:3. Honest classification — if uncertain, default to UPSTREAM-CLAIM (under-probing has higher false-PASS cost than over-probing)
91:
92:**Distinguishes from §Reporting categories above**: §Reporting categories classifies REPORT shape (OVER/UNDER/HNF — about agent's output). §Subclaim-type discriminator classifies SOURCE shape (UPSTREAM/OPERATIONAL/CATEGORY — about what's being verified). Orthogonal axes — a UPSTREAM-CLAIM probe may produce HNF, OVER, or UNDER report.
93:
94:## Output-form verification modifier (SHAPE-CLAIM)
95:
96:After typing the subclaim by source as UPSTREAM / OPERATIONAL / CATEGORY, add **SHAPE-CLAIM** when the claim depends on **structured output that can be checked before deployment**: TypeScript workflow code, Pydantic / BaseModel payloads, Zod / Effect schemas, JSON Schema validated tool args, `PINS.json` entries, `settings.json` hook entries, `.mcp.json` server configs, MCP tool args, or hook JSONL payloads.
97:
98:**SHAPE-CLAIM is a MODIFIER, not a source type.** It combines with each source class:
99:- `UPSTREAM-CLAIM + SHAPE-CLAIM`: PINS.json bumps citing upstream HEAD SHA + content-SHA (the bump is upstream-state; the content shape is checkable)
100:- `OPERATIONAL-CLAIM + SHAPE-CLAIM`: settings.json hook entries, .mcp.json server configs, hook JSONL payloads (the hook fires per harness state; the JSON shape validates)
101:- `CATEGORY-CLAIM + SHAPE-CLAIM`: agent frontmatter or skill SKILL.md (the frontmatter is structured + parseable; the categorical role is semantic)
102:
103:**Probe rule**: run the strongest available compile/schema/validation check first. If it passes, downgrade only **shape-refutation budget**; still run semantic/runtime probes for side effects, credentials, provider limitations, type coercion, `any`/untyped fields, unsupported schema keywords, and producer/consumer boundary mismatches. **Compile-pass is NOT deploy-pass.**
104:
105:**Convergence-gate evidence** (per `.claude/rules/convergence-gate.md`):
106:- **Axis 1** (≥3 T1 sources from distinct orgs) — **PASS**:
107:  1. **n8n MCP TypeScript-output** (`blog.n8n.io/n8n-mcp-server/` 2026-04-29 [VERIFIED 2026-05-02]) — "Generates code, not JSON ... must type-check and compile before anything touches your instance"
108:  2. **Effect Schema** (`effect.website/docs/schema/introduction/` [VERIFIED 2026-05-02]) — TypeScript `Schema<Type, Encoded, Requirements>` + `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` compile-time enforcement; "the type checker will catch any attempt to assign an invalid value"
109:  3. **Pydantic v2** (`pydantic.dev/docs/validation/latest/get-started/why/` [VERIFIED 2026-05-02]) — Python type hints as schema specification; `BaseModel` core primitive; dual-purpose IDE static analysis + runtime validation + JSON Schema generation
110:- **Axis 2** (≥2 named T2 practitioners with dated artifact) — **PARTIAL**: creator/maintainer endorsements (Samuel Colvin / Michael Arnaldi / n8n vendor representative) + official docs are close to but not equal to the dated-practitioner-artifact-citing-this-specific-pattern evidence shape required by convergence-gate Axis 2. Re-evaluate when an independent named-T2 dated artifact citing the specific compile-before-deploy pattern lands.
111:- **Axis 3** (≥3 months stability) — **PASS**: Pydantic v2 ~2.5y, Effect Schema ~5y; n8n MCP TypeScript-output substrate mature (the workflow-build feature is new but the TypeScript-as-schema substrate is not).
112:
113:**Anti-patterns** (per codex T1 F-002 + Q7 prescription):
114:- **Free-form JSON when a schema/compiler exists** — n8n catches this; "code beats JSON" for LLM-emitted structured output
115:- **Compile-pass treated as deploy-pass** — Effect docs warn: `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` runtime mismatch is possible if the compiler flag is disabled
116:- **Type hints without runtime validation at untrusted boundaries** — Pydantic validators are runtime-separate; type hints alone don't validate user input
117:- **`any`, `dict[str, Any]`, permissive JSON Schema, missing `additionalProperties: false` treated as strong shape proof** — these are escape hatches that nullify the gate
118:- **Schema generated but not actually used at the producer/consumer boundary** — generation without enforcement is a documentation comment, not a gate
119:- **Provider-constrained schema accepted without post-parse validation against the original schema** — Anthropic structured-outputs simplifies schemas at the API boundary; post-parse validation against the original schema closes the gap

60:## Risk-stratified verification gating
61:
62:# Reference: `https://resources.anthropic.com/2026-agentic-coding-trends-report` (TIER-1 Anthropic; full PDF at `https://resources.anthropic.com/hubfs/2026%20Agentic%20Coding%20Trends%20Report.pdf`) [VERIFIED 2026-05-03 via Wave-6 Agent M perplexity_research [17][31][48]] — Anthropic 2026 Agentic Coding Trends Report identifies risk-stratified gating as SOTA pattern: low-risk = full-agent-delegate + post-commit review; medium-risk = pre-commit human review; high-risk = design review BEFORE agent implements.
63:# Reference: Wave-6 Agent M Round-4 task design at `tmp/wave6-agent-m-sota-git-practice-2026-05-03.md:165-196` (ADOPT-NOW conf=0.92; cohort attribution C5 named-author Anthropic; Axis 1+2+3 PASS via STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS predicate).
64:
65:Beyond the **finding-severity** taxonomy above (which classifies what codex found AFTER work landed), the **task risk-class** axis classifies the change BEFORE work begins. Both axes are orthogonal — severity describes findings (P0/P1/P2/P3); risk-class describes tasks (low/medium/high). Both inform the T0-T7 lifecycle gate selection.
66:
67:### The 3-tier risk taxonomy + T0-T7 gate mapping
68:
69:| Risk class | Task signature | Verification gate | sss T0-T7 mapping |
70:|---|---|---|---|
71:| **Low-risk** | Reversible operations on isolated surfaces (tests / docs / non-cardinal-rule edits / bounded scripts ≤200 LOC); single-axis-change with clear primary-source backing | Full-agent-delegate + **post-commit review only** (T3 PostToolUse `Bash(git commit *)`) | T1 SKIP per `codex-t1-fix-forward-pattern.md §Mechanical-mirror exception` IF predicates met; else light T1 + T3 verify |
72:| **Medium-risk** | Multi-file ships / new mechanics / behavioral changes / existing-surface edits with potential ripple; rule-layer or skill-layer additions ≤200 LOC | Pre-commit cross-model review (**T2 commit-time hook** at `Bash(git commit *)` PreToolUse — agent implements, codex GPT-5.5 reviews uncommitted tree before commit lands) | T1 pre-edit + T2 working-tree + T3 post-commit (full lifecycle) |
73:| **High-risk** | Cardinal-rule surface edits (CLAUDE.md / `.claude/settings.json` / `.mcp.json` / cardinal-rules-defining `.claude/rules/*.md`) / security-class operations / destructive Bash / >200 LOC architectural changes / new T-touchpoint or wedge-class introduction | **Design review BEFORE agent implements** (T0 candidate-list challenge + T1 deep-review-exec xhigh + T5 plan-stage; multi-cohort fan-out + Probe-DAG harness-fit verification BEFORE T1 fires) | T0 + T5 (pre-design) + T1 + T2 + T3 + T4 + T6 — full 7-touchpoint coverage |
74:
75:### How to apply
76:
77:1. **Classify task risk-class FIRST** (BEFORE writing T1 consult or scoping the ship):
78:   - Examine target file class (cardinal-rule surface? rule-layer? script? test?)
79:   - Examine LOC delta (≤200 LOC bounded vs >200 LOC architectural)
80:   - Examine reversibility (pure additive doc-only? behavioral mechanism change? security/destructive?)
81:   - Examine cite-class novelty (new TIER-1/TIER-2 source class introduced? new cite anchor pattern?)
82:2. **Select gate-set per risk-class** (per The 3-tier risk taxonomy table above)
83:3. **Document risk-class in commit body** — include `risk-class: low | medium | high` line + 1-line classification rationale (e.g., `risk-class: medium — multi-file rule edit + new mechanics introduced; T1+T2+T3 lifecycle invoked`)
84:4. **Risk-class is REVISABLE pre-commit** — if T1 surfaces unanticipated cardinal-surface impact, upgrade to high-risk and fire T0+T5 retroactively before commit
85:
86:### Anti-patterns
87:
88:- **"All changes go through medium-risk gate"** — refuted by Anthropic taxonomy. Low-risk operations are over-gated by medium-risk T1+T2 coverage. Conversely, high-risk operations are under-gated by medium-risk-only T1+T2 — they need T0 candidate-list challenge + T5 plan-stage review BEFORE T1 fires.
89:- **Risk-class as severity proxy** — they're orthogonal axes. A low-risk ship can produce a P0 finding. A high-risk ship can produce only P3 findings. Don't conflate.
90:- **Static risk-class declaration without re-classification trigger** — if T1/T2 surfaces unanticipated cardinal-surface ripple, the original low-risk classification is invalid; re-classify, do NOT silently proceed.

64:```

22:## Pattern signature
23:
24:- Stage 1 — **Wire**: audit hook configured to fire on a commit/event matcher (typically `Bash(git commit *)` PostToolUse, or SessionEnd, or an external cadence).
25:- Stage 2 — **Surface**: audit JSONL accumulates drift records (`any_drift: true`) without consumer action.
26:- Stage 3 — **Close**: a /loop fire ships a surgical edit that updates the drifted axis with provenance (SHA + cycle attribution).
27:- Stage 4 — **Re-fire**: the next audit run produces `any_drift: false` for that axis, confirming closure.
28:
29:## Hook telemetry contract — agent_id/agent_type propagation
30:
31:**Reference**: `Z:/repos/deps/claude-agent-sdk-python/src/claude_agent_sdk/types.py:246-262,265,274,284,344 @ HEAD b512f256450dba8f0dd1399e485563b7deb9c534 [VERIFIED 2026-05-02 via Ship 38 Marker Decay refresh; Wave 9 audit at agent af32addc used 8348d1f8 — cited line ranges UNCHANGED in 8348d1f8..b512f256 16-commit span per Ship 38 diff probe (types.py +8 SandboxNetworkConfig at L783-806; subprocess_cli.py 22-mod stderr-reader; client.py + __init__.py UNCHANGED)]` — TIER-1 OFFICIAL Anthropic SDK `_SubagentContextMixin` TypedDict mandates `agent_id: str` + `agent_type: str` on the **four tool-lifecycle hook inputs** (`PreToolUseHookInput` `:265`, `PostToolUseHookInput` `:274`, `PostToolUseFailureHookInput` `:284`, `PermissionRequestHookInput` `:344` — all inherit the mixin). Verbatim source comment at `:252`: "When multiple sub-agents run in parallel their tool-lifecycle hooks interleave over the same control channel — this is the only reliable way to attribute each one to the correct sub-agent."
32:
33:### The contract (forward-only invariant)
34:
35:Every JSONL-emitting hook in `.claude/hooks/scripts/*.py` MUST persist these two fields when present in hook input:
36:
37:```json
38:{
39:  "ts": "2026-04-30T...",
40:  "agent_id": "<uuid-or-null-if-main-agent>",
41:  "agent_type": "<sota-researcher | code-reviewer | codex-rescue | ... | null>",
42:  "tool_name": "...",
43:  ...
44:}
45:```
46:
47:**Hook stdin JSON should be read at TOP LEVEL**: `payload.get("agent_id")` and `payload.get("agent_type")`. The SDK comment indicates the CLI derives those values from an internal tool-use context, but hook scripts should NOT expect a nested `tool_use_context` object unless live runtime capture proves one exists (per codex T1 F-002 fix-forward 2026-04-30 — earlier orchestrator paraphrase of `tool_use_context.agent_id` was incorrect).
48:
49:### Why agent_id is load-bearing
50:
51:When sss runs 3-6 parallel agents per `.claude/rules/parallel-agent-wave.md`, all of their PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure/PermissionRequest hooks fire on the same control channel. Without `agent_id`, JSONL records interleave anonymously:
52:
53:```
54:{"ts":"...", "tool_name":"Edit", "file_path":"X.md"}    ← agent A or agent B?
55:{"ts":"...", "tool_name":"Edit", "file_path":"Y.md"}    ← agent A or agent B?
56:```
57:
58:§Stage 3 Close discipline above requires attributing drift to a specific agent for surgical fix-forward. Without `agent_id`, fix-forward becomes guesswork.
59:
